SOLVED:      Executing a large order (e.g., sell 10,000 ETH) in one transaction causes      significant price impact. TWAP execution splits it into smaller slices      spread over time, reducing market impact and achieving a better average price.      This is a common need in institutional and whale trading that lacks a clean      open-source implementation on CoW Protocol.HOW IT WORKS:      1. Caller creates a TwapOrder specifying token, total amount, slice count,         and minimum interval between slices.      2. The full amount is pulled from the caller immediately and held in escrow.      3. Anyone (a keeper, the owner, or a bot) calls executeSlice() with the         CoW orderUid for that slice. The slice is settled via CoW Protocol.      4. Slices execute at most once per `intervalSeconds`. The order completes         when all slices are executed. The owner can cancel at any time for a refund.SECURITY:      - executeSlice() is permissionless (anyone can execute). This is intentional:        it allows keeper bots to execute slices without owner involvement.        The minAmountOutPerSlice guard protects against sandwiching each slice.      - Tokens are held in escrow (not sent to CoW up front). Cancellation is safe.      - ReentrancyGuard + CEI pattern on all state-modifying functions.      - The CoW orderUid must be generated off-chain via the CoW API matching the        exact amountPerSlice. This contract does NOT validate orderUid contents \u2014        CoW's settlement contract enforces them.KNOWN LIMITATION:      Full integration testing requires a live CoW Protocol solver. Unit tests use      mock relayer and settler contracts. cancelTwapOrder(uint256).details: Only the order owner can cancel. Remaining (unexecuted) tokens are      returned to the owner. Already-executed slices are not affected.

createTwapOrder(address,uint256,uint256,.details: Pulls the full totalAmount from msg.sender into this contract (escrow).      Does NOT require owner to pre-approve the relayer — each slice approves      and resets individually to limit approval surface.

params.intervalSeconds: Minimum seconds between consecutive slice executions.
params.minAmountOutPerSlice: Minimum output per slice (slippage guard passed to CoW).
params.sliceCount: Number of equal slices to split the order into.
params.token: ERC-20 token to sell via CoW.
params.totalAmount: Total amount to sell across all slices.

returns.orderId: The ID of the created TWAP order.

executeSlice(uint256,bytes).details: Permissionless: anyone can execute. The minAmountOutPerSlice parameter      on the CoW order (set at creation time) protects against sandwich attacks      on individual slices.      The caller provides a CoW orderUid obtained from the CoW Protocol API.      The orderUid must correspond to a sell order for exactly amountPerSlice      of the TWAP token. CoW's settlement contract enforces this — if the      orderUid does not match, the settle() call will revert.

params.orderUid: The CoW Protocol orderUid for this slice (obtained off-chain from CoW API).

cancelTwapOrder(uint256).notice: Cancel a TWAP order and refund remaining tokens to the owner.         Only callable by the order owner.

createTwapOrder(address,uint256,uint256,.notice: Create a new TWAP order. Pulls the full token amount upfront.

executeSlice(uint256,bytes).notice: Execute the next pending slice of a TWAP order via CoW Protocol.         Anyone may call this after the interval has elapsed.

getOrder(uint256).notice: Get the full state of a TWAP order.

isSliceReady(uint256).notice: Returns true if the next slice of an order is ready to execute.

totalOrders().notice: Total number of orders ever created.
